title: Kuwae (Tombuk) eruption
summary: A large, mostly submarine eruption in the Shepherd Islands of central Vanuatu around AD 1452, known locally as the Tombuk eruption, destroyed the island of Kuwae and left a submarine caldera between Epi and Tongoa. Witter and Self estimated 30 to 60 km3 of dacite magma and a very large sulphur aerosol load; its exact date and global climate signal remain debated.

uncertainty.note: Witter and Self give AD 1452 with ice-core acidity peaks over 1453 to 1457; Ballard and colleagues note other ice-core studies at AD 1453, two events in the 1450s, and doubts that the event is earlier or later than the 1450s.

where.modern_name: Kuwae submarine caldera between Epi and Tongoa, Shefa Province, Vanuatu
where.historical_name: Kuwae island, Shepherd Islands, central Vanuatu (no state)

importance.justification: One of the largest atmospheric sulphate events of the past millennium in the widely held view, and it split an inhabited island.
